penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: One-time template/boilerplate sales and cohort courses require high volume of individual buyers (hundreds per launch) to generate meaningful recurring revenue; a single solo operator without an existing audience will struggle to reach critical mass.

rationale: Solo founders do pay for starter kits ($49-199 one-time) and there is a clear buyer, but the business model is a content/template product that needs ongoing audience-building and repeated launch cycles to sustain revenue — not the kind of always-on autonomous service this factory is optimised to run. One-time sales to individual indie hackers mean the operator must keep marketing continuously rather than building a recurring-revenue base. The penalty for b2c-at-scale brings total below validate threshold. Better suited to a creator with an existing audience; not a strong factory play.
solution_plan: Not the strongest fit for this factory. The product — a paid Next.js + Claude API starter kit or a cohort-based course — is genuinely buildable (Claude can generate and document a boilerplate; a Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy page handles sales), but sustained revenue requires continuous content marketing, community presence, and launch-cycle management that a solo operator without an existing following cannot automate away. If Youval already has a developer audience or newsletter, this is worth a quick validate (ship a $79 Gumroad template, see if 10 people buy in the first week without paid ads). Without that audience, the customer-acquisition problem outweighs the build simplicity.
notes: Total after penalty (4.7) is below min_total_to_validate (5.5). build_gates for operational_autonomy (6, at the floor but not above) and buyer_clarity (6, at floor) are borderline. Primary issue is the b2c-at-scale model and lack of existing audience to drive one-time sales.
